Call this quietly when the user shares something personal worth keeping: their name, job, location, preferences ("I'm vegetarian"), ongoing projects, names of pets/family/friends, things they love or hate, or anything they'd expect you to recall days from now. Keep each fact to one short sentence phrased as a standalone note ("user's dog is named Max", "user prefers dark mode"). Do NOT call for small talk, transient questions, one-off jokes, or facts already obvious from the current conversation. Do not save the same fact twice.

The query should be a few words capturing the topic ("server crash debugging", "my sister's wedding"), not the user's full sentence. Use the returned summaries as fuzzy memory to inform your reply — don't quote them verbatim or list them as bullets. If nothing comes back, say so honestly instead of making something up.

topic.description: A few words capturing the topic to recall, e.g. 'server crash debugging' or 'my sister's wedding'. Not the user's full sentence.

Call this quietly when the user shares something personal worth keeping: their name, job, location, preferences ("I'm vegetarian"), ongoing projects, names of pets/family/friends, things they love or hate, or anything they'd expect you to recall days from now. Keep each fact to one short sentence phrased as a standalone note ("user's dog is named Max", "user prefers dark mode"). Do NOT call for small talk, transient questions, one-off jokes, or facts already obvious from the current conversation. Do not save the same fact twice.

fact.description: One short sentence about the user phrased as a standalone note, e.g. "user's dog is named Max" or "user prefers dark mode".

schemas_sent.name: recall
schemas_sent.description: recall("topic") — Look up summaries of past conversations that touched on a topic. Call this when the user references something from before that you don't see in the current chat: "remember when we...", "last time we talked about...", "that thing I told you about my X", "did I ever mention...", or any question about past events/projects/feelings that aren't in this conversation's history. The query should be a few words capturing the topic ("server crash debugging", "my sister's wedding"), not the user's full sentence. Use the returned summaries as fuzzy memory to inform your reply — don't quote them verbatim or list them as bullets. If nothing comes back, say so honestly instead of making something up.

topic.description: A few words capturing the topic to recall, e.g. 'server crash debugging' or 'my sister's wedding'. Not the user's full sentence.
